<strong>Comprueba Euler con un caso cono: Check Euler with a known case. A cube gives $8 - 12 + 6 = 2$. If your count of a new figure does not give what it should for its genus, the error is in the count.
<strong>El exceso angular es área.</stro: Angular excess is area. On the sphere, what a triangle has over $180°$ is proportional to its area. That single sentence solves several questions in the first section.
<strong>En topología no se mide: se cuen: In topology you do not measure: you count. Holes, components, faces. If a question seems to ask for a length, you have to look for the invariant that does not depend on it.
<strong>Pregúntate siempre en qué superf: Always ask yourself which surface you are on. Nearly every answer changes sign between the sphere, the plane and the hyperbolic plane; writing down the curvature at the start avoids answering with the wrong geometry.
Al revés: cuanto más pequeño es un trián: The other way round: the smaller a spherical triangle is, the more it resembles a flat one and the less excess it has. The one with three right angles is enormous, an eighth of the sphere.
Cada tramo aporta un número fijo de preg: Each section contributes a fixed number of questions, drawn at random from its topics without repeating a topic while that is possible, and avoiding the most basic exercises. With 3 topics and 5 questions, one exam covers almost the whole block: that is why the link at the end reproduces the same exam, and “another exam” draws a different one.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
Decidir si dos figuras son homeomorfas;: Deciding whether two figures are homeomorphic; counting holes; computing the Euler characteristic of a polyhedron or of a triangulation and using it to tell surfaces apart.
Durante dos mil años, intentar demostrar: For two thousand years, trying to prove Euclid's fifth postulate was an examination exercise nobody passed. Saccheri published a whole book in 1733 of absurd consequences of denying it, convinced he was reducing it to absurdity; in fact he was writing the first theorems of hyperbolic geometry without realising. What is asked here as an exercise was, for centuries, the most famous open problem in mathematics.
El enlace de un examen corregido reprodu: The link to a marked exam reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and will be able to compare results and procedures.
Elige los tramos que entran. Las pregunt: Choose the sections to include. The questions are drawn at random from the exercises of each topic in the block, avoiding the most basic ones and without repeating a topic while possible. There are no hints: the marking and the step-by-step solution come on submitting.
Es el octante: dos meridianos separados: It is the octant: two meridians $90°$ apart and a piece of the equator. The excess of $90°$ measures exactly one eighth of the sphere.
Eso vale en el plano, y solo porque se a: That holds in the plane, and only because the fifth postulate is granted. On a curved surface it stops being true, and that is what the block is about.
No: los ángulos de un triángulo suman si: No: the angles of a triangle always add up to $180°$
Otra idea de recta: Another idea of a straight line
Suma de los ángulos de un triángulo en l: The sum of the angles of a triangle on the sphere and in the hyperbolic plane; angular excess and area; the curvature of a curve and of a surface; geodesics and the theorema egregium.
Sí, pero solo si el triángulo es muy peq: Yes, but only if the triangle is very small
Sí: en la esfera los ángulos suman más d: Yes: on the sphere the angles add up to more than $180°$, and this one adds to $270°$
Tres temas que ponen en duda las reglas: Three topics that call into question the rules everything in the [[ge-angulos|geometry]] block was measured with: what happens if parallels meet, how you measure what bends, and what is left of a figure once you stop measuring. This topic teaches nothing new: it asks. A procedural exam with exercises from the whole block, with a clock and no hints.
Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock paper taken at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the 3 topics of the block, spread across sections, and every time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submission everything is marked, the step-by-step solution of each question opens, and the mark comes out section by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not solved yet: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
Un triángulo dibujado sobre una esfera t: A triangle drawn on a sphere has three right angles. Is that possible?
